data.title: A2 Level Check
data.description: A mixed grammar check to estimate whether the learner is working securely at CEFR A2 level.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct present simple sentence.
sections.explain: With 'he', 'she' or 'it' in the present simple, the verb normally ends in -s. The correct form is 'works'.

words.word: She works in a hospital.
She work in a hospital.
She working in a hospital.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence for an action happening now.
sections.explain: For an action happening now, use 'am/is/are' + verb-ing. The correct form is 'is talking'.

words.word: He is talking on the phone now.
He talks on the phone now.
He is talk on the phone now.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct past simple sentence.

words.word: We went to London last weekend.
We goed to London last weekend.
We have gone to London last weekend.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct question in the past simple.
sections.explain: Past simple questions use 'did' + the base form of the verb. The correct form is 'Did you see...?'.

words.word: Did you see the film yesterday?
Did you saw the film yesterday?
Saw you the film yesterday?

sections.explain: The comparative form of 'expensive' is 'more expensive'.

words.word: This hotel is more expensive than the other one.
This hotel is expensiver than the other one.
This hotel is more expensive that the other one.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct expression for a future plan.
sections.explain: Use 'am/is/are going to' + base verb to talk about a future plan. The correct form is 'are going to visit'.

words.word: We are going to visit my parents tomorrow.
We going to visit my parents tomorrow.
We are going visit my parents tomorrow.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct modal verb structure.
sections.explain: After a modal verb such as 'should', use the base form of the verb without 'to'. The correct form is 'should drink'.

words.word: You should drink more water.
You should to drink more water.
You should drinking more water.

sections.explain: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun, so we say 'some advice', not 'an advice' or 'many advices'.

words.word: She gave me some useful advice.
She gave me an useful advice.
She gave me many useful advices.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct present perfect sentence.
sections.explain: Use 'have/has' + past participle to talk about life experience when no finished past time is given. The correct form is 'have visited'.

words.word: I have visited Spain three times.
I have visit Spain three times.
I am visited Spain three times.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using 'since' and 'for'.
sections.explain: Use 'for' with a period of time and the present perfect for a situation that started in the past and continues now. The correct form is 'have lived here for three years'.

words.word: I have lived here for three years.
I live here since three years.
I have lived here since three years.
